transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Zenith IT Sec), Lena (Platform Eng), Marcus (Dir Infra)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance-focused review covering SSO (SAML) integration patterns, SCIM provisioning/group sync, role mapping/least-privilege proposals, audit log retention, and encryption/KMS questions. Agreed to pilot with staging IdP and share role-mapping templates.

Topics (auto):
- SAML attribute mapping and SP metadata
- SCIM group sync and deprovisioning flows
- RBAC templates: admin/engineer/viewer/service-accounts
- Audit logs retention, export, and SIEM integration
- Encryption at rest KMS/HSM options and key separation

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Uh, we'll keep this focused on SSO and role mapping patterns, Priya and I will walk through our typical recommend approach and then get into specifics for your IdP. Carlos, Lena, Marcus, anything to add before we hop in?

[00:22] Carlos: No, that's good. We mainly want to validate that user provisioning and deprovisioning won't leave backdoors, and we have to map to our least privilege policies. Also SOC 2 questions but I think Jordan will share the report.

[00:40] Priya: Yep, we'll drop the SOC 2 summary. Quick note, our usual integration channels are SAML for authentication and SCIM for provisioning, we do support JIT (just in time) provisioning via SAML assertion as well but the recommended enterprise flow is SAML + SCIM group sync for predictable role mapping.

[01:05] Lena: Quick clarification, when you say SCIM group sync, do you do two-way or read-only? We currently have groups as the source of truth in Okta.

[01:20] Priya: Good question. Typical pattern: read-only SCIM from IdP into Redwood (our service) — IdP is source of truth. We support group patch/put operations in SCIM v2.0 and map SCIM groups to role templates. We don't push changes back to IdP. There are some customer-specific webhook flows for more advanced cases but not common.

[01:45] Marcus: And how quickly does deprovisioning propagate? We need near-immediate revocation when someone leaves.

[01:52] Priya: On SCIM group change events we process within seconds — tongue-in-cheek network delay aside — but worst case minutes. We also have a periodic reconciliation job for drift. If the account is disabled in SCIM, our session revocation can be triggered and active tokens invalidated; we can also reduce session TTLs during the pilot if you prefer aggressive short sessions.

[02:20] Jordan: I'll just flag that if you need stricter session invalidation we can set shorter token lifetimes for the pilot. We'll document recommended TTLs.

[02:35] Carlos: Good. On the RBAC side we're thinking three main roles: Admin, Platform Engineer, and ReadOnly. We also have some machine/service accounts. How do you recommend mapping those in SCIM?

[02:50] Priya: Common approach: map SCIM groups to role templates; e.g., SCIM group 'zenith-admins' -> role 'org_admin' with limited permissions (we keep admin scope narrow), 'zenith-platform' -> role 'engineer' with deploy and model ops rights, 'zenith-readonly' -> viewer. Service accounts we recommend as JWT-based service identities with explicit key rotation and HSM-backed keys if you need KMS separation.

[03:20] Lena: Can you share an example role-mapping JSON? The engineering team likes to see exact attribute names.

[03:27] Priya: Yep, we'll provide a template. It includes attributes like 'role_id', 'permissions', 'scim_group_filter' and optional scoping to projects/environments. Example: { "role_id": "engineer", "permissions": ["deploy","view_logs"], "scim_group": "zenith-platform" } — note that's simplified, we'll send full schema.

[03:55] Marcus: About least-privilege: do you support time-bound elevated access? We sometimes grant temporary admin for incidents.

[04:05] Priya: We do. Two patterns: (1) ephemeral roles via our console with approval flow (manual) or (2) time-limited role assignments through SCIM patch operations; for the latter you can have an external orchestration system add the user to the 'temp-admins' group and SCIM will map it. We'll include recommended audit hooks and approver logging.

[04:32] Carlos: Audit logs — how long do you retain them, and can we export them to our SIEM? We have a 7-year retention policy for certain events.

[04:45] Jordan: Redwood keeps detailed audit logs. The default retention on hosted plans is 90 days, enterprise customers can configure longer retention and export to S3 or push to SIEM via a connector. We'll include the export docs, and Priya can show the event types that are logged.

[05:05] Priya: Event types include auth events, token grants/revocations, SCIM provisioning events (create/update/patch), role assignments, and admin actions like policy changes. We also emit structured JSON that your SIEM can ingest. Retention beyond default is an enterprise add-on — retention policies can be configured per account.

[05:32] Lena: For audit integrity, do you have an append-only store or signed logs? We want to ensure tamper evidence.

[05:40] Priya: Good point. We support write-once object storage for audit exports and can sign exports using our KMS-backed keys. Internally our event store is append-first; for forensic requirements we typically recommend exporting to your S3 with object-lock or sending to a third-party WORM storage. We'll document recommended practices.

[06:05] Marcus: Encryption — we need keys to be customer-controlled for some workloads. What's possible?

[06:13] Jordan: We support two models: Redwood-managed encryption keys (default) and customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS in your cloud account or HSM for Private deployments. For Private/VPC installs we can integrate with your HSM/KMS and keys never leave your control.

[06:33] Priya: For hosted, CMK integration is possible via cross-account KMS grants where you keep control of the root key; our service encrypts data at rest using those keys. We can share the technical steps and IAM perms needed.

[06:50] Carlos: Does that include KV cache and model artifacts? We have IP concerns.

[06:56] Priya: Yes, customer-managed keys can be used to encrypt model artifacts, persisted KV caches, and workspace data. Runtime in-memory caches are, of course, in memory but disk-backed caches and logs will be encrypted. For absolute separation, Private deployment is the recommended route.

[07:20] Jordan: Let's pivot back to SAML attributes — we need to agree on which attributes Redwood expects for role mapping and for JIT provisioning.

[07:29] Priya: We typically expect email, name, and optionally an attribute for groups like 'groups' claim. For JIT provisioning, SAML assertion should include email and displayName. For SCIM-based provisioning this is less critical since SCIM is canonical. For role mapping via SAML-only scenarios we use an attribute like 'roles' or a namespace such as 'urn:zenith:roles' if your IdP supports custom attrs.

[07:58] Lena: Our Okta team currently emits groups in the SAML assertion as 'groups', but sometimes group names have org prefixes. Can we support regex mapping?

[08:10] Priya: Yes, we support regex-based mapping and prefix stripping in our role templates. We'll include examples like '^zenith-(.*)$' -> '$1'.

[08:25] Marcus: On SCIM — does Redwood support incremental patch operations and filtering to only sync specific groups? We don't want thousands of groups imported.

[08:34] Priya: Absolutely. SCIM filter queries can be used to limit groups; additionally we support group include/exclude lists in the config. We process PATCH and PUT for user/group updates and can handle large directories without pulling everything if you scope it.

[08:50] Carlos: Are there limits on SCIM throughput? Our directory has spikes during offboarding runs.

[08:58] Priya: We rate-limit SCIM traffic to protect downstream systems; typical enterprise throughput is fine but for huge bulk changes we recommend a staged approach or contacting us to request a temporary increase. For offboarding spikes we can whitelist or queue.

[09:18] Jordan: One question for you — any regulatory data residency concerns? I remember you have EU manufacturing sites.

[09:26] Marcus: Yes, EU and NA separation required for some telemetry. We need customer metadata and logs for EU accounts to stay in EU regions.

[09:34] Priya: We support region-bound accounts; hosted customers can provision instances in EU regions. Audit logs and backups can be configured to stay in region. For full guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where you can pin the region and storage.

[09:52] Lena: For SAML testing, will you accept a test IdP from our side? We can provision an Okta dev tenant.

[09:58] Jordan: Yes please. That would be ideal — Lena, if you can provide a test tenant and an engineer with admin rights we'll use that for the staging test.

[10:08] Carlos: About service accounts: are they visible in audit logs with their key fingerprints? We need to map actions to service identities.

[10:16] Priya: Service accounts have their own identity entries and keys; we emit the service_account id in audit events and include key fingerprint in the metadata. You can also tag service accounts with owner/team attributes.

[10:34] Marcus: Encryption key rotation — how often and who performs it? Can we rotate without downtime?

[10:41] Priya: With CMK model, you control rotation cadence. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate regularly and support key rotation without downtime via envelope encryption patterns. For CMK where keys are in your KMS, rotation is subject to KMS capabilities — we use key aliases to avoid needing downtime.

[11:05] Jordan: Coming back to least-privilege, one common concern is privilege creep over time. We recommend periodic reviews and we can attach policy expiration tags to role assignments.

[11:18] Carlos: Do you have a UI for permission reviews or an API we can call to enumerate current mappings?

[11:25] Priya: Both. We have a permissions matrix export and an API endpoint that lists users, roles, and group memberships which you can query and pull into your governance tooling. We'll provide the API spec.

[11:44] Lena: About SAML metadata — what's required in the SP metadata you will send?

[11:50] Jordan: We'll send an SP metadata bundle including ACS URL, entityID, and our signing certificate. Priya: Also note we can accept either SHA-1 or SHA-256 cert fingerprints but recommend SHA-256.

[12:05] Priya: One more gotcha we've seen: if your IdP strips nameIDs or uses transient nameIDs, JIT provisioning can fail. We recommend email as persistent NameID or include 'subject' in the assertion.

[12:22] Marcus: For our compliance reviewers, they'll likely want to see a mapping doc that ties SCIM groups to least-privilege roles and who has access. Can you produce a draft matrix?

[12:31] Jordan: Yes we'll produce a sample matrix; Priya will draft the role descriptions.

[12:37] Carlos: If we do a pilot, what's the rollback path if something misbehaves? For example an errant SCIM sync that adds people to admin group.

[12:45] Priya: We have a soft-sync/dry-run mode for SCIM that you can enable — it will show changes without applying them. Additionally, role changes are auditable and reversible; we can also temporarily lock role modifications while you run acceptance tests. We'll include rollback playbooks.

[13:10] Lena: About SIEM integration — which event fields do you emit? We want timestamp, user_id, action, source_ip, service_account_id, and any role meta.

[13:22] Priya: Yes, all that and more: event_type, resource_id, request_id, change_summary. We also include raw SAML assertion snippets (redacted) for debugging if you opt in.

[13:36] Carlos: Do you support field-level redaction for exported logs? We sometimes need to mask PII.

[13:43] Priya: You can configure redaction policies on export. By default we redact sensitive tokens; you can define fields to strip or pseudonymize before export. We'll share doc links.

[14:00] Jordan: Switching gears — any specific SOC 2 or ISO questions?

[14:06] Carlos: SOC 2 scope — is SSO in scope and are audit trails included? Our auditors will want to see control mappings.

[14:15] Jordan: Yes SSO and audit trails are in scope for our SOC 2. We'll share the SOC 2 summary and a mapping doc that shows the relevant controls. For higher-assurance needs we can schedule an attestation call with security.

[14:30] Marcus: Do you run regular pentests and vulnerability scans? Our procurement team asks for that.

[14:36] Priya: We run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party penetration tests; we can share redacted reports under NDA. We also publish CVE responses and patching cadence.

[14:55] Lena: Any limitations on SAML audiences or multiple SP endpoints per account? We have multi-tenant apps internally.

[15:03] Priya: We support multiple ACS URLs and audience restrictions; let us know exact flows and we can model them.

[15:18] Carlos: A small question on metadata rotation — if your signing cert rotates, how do we handle the trust?

[15:24] Priya: We rotate keys with advance notification and support dual certs for a transition window. We'll include an operational plan in the notes.

[15:40] Jordan: I want to call out a few edge cases we've seen: (1) SCIM group name changes and how our mapping handles them, (2) nested groups in Okta — we flatten membership but can also respect nested semantics if you prefer, (3) service accounts created outside SCIM — those need explicit tagging.

[15:58] Marcus: Nested groups are used a lot by our BU leads, flattening is fine if you document it.

[16:07] Priya: We'll include examples of nested-group handling and recommended group naming conventions to avoid surprises.

[16:20] Carlos: For the pilot, what's success criteria? We propose: (a) IdP integration completed, (b) SCIM provisioning for pilot users working, (c) role mapping applied and verified, (d) audit log export validated. Thoughts?

[16:34] Jordan: That's perfect. We'll add a latency check for auth flows and a security checklist.

[16:42] Lena: One small item: can we limit SSO for certain routes? Some internal tools shouldn't be exposed via SSO.

[16:49] Priya: You can configure route-level access controls and per-route RBAC. We'll show how to scope routes to roles or IP allowlists.

[17:05] Carlos: Anything in your config that might cause a silent permission escalation? We want to avoid surprises.

[17:12] Priya: No silent escalation. Role precedence is explicit — we evaluate the most permissive role assignment but we'll surface conflicts in the UI and API. We'll also recommend a deny-by-default posture in the pilot.

[17:30] Marcus: For the pilot, how do we manage secrets for service accounts? Where are they stored?

[17:36] Priya: Stored encrypted in our secrets store; if you prefer CMK/HSM-backed secrets we can route through your KMS. We also support short-lived credentials for service accounts via a token exchange.

[17:55] Jordan: We're nearing the middle of the call, sounds like we've captured the key items. Any blockers from your side?

[18:03] Lena: Only getting the dev Okta tenant and deciding on the pilot users. We'll do that this week.

[18:10] Carlos: Also need to include procurement on the SOC2 docs but that's not blocking integration.

[18:18] Jordan: Great. Priya, can you outline the exact artifacts we'll send?

[18:23] Priya: Sure: (1) SP metadata bundle, (2) role-mapping JSON template, (3) SCIM config examples and filter samples, (4) SOC 2 summary and the security overview slide, (5) audit export example and SIEM field map.

[18:45] Marcus: Can you also include an example of rollback steps for a bad SCIM sync?

[18:50] Priya: Yes — dry-run, snap export, revert via API, lock roles, and contact Redwood support. We'll add that to the playbook.

[19:05] Jordan: Any other competitors you're evaluating? Carlos?

[19:08] Carlos: We're looking at BigCloudAI for hosted and ShelfServe for a more platform approach but both had some concerns with RBAC granularity.

[19:18] Priya: Noted, we'll highlight differences in the follow-up doc.

[19:26] Lena: One last tech question — do you allow SCIM filtering by user attribute (e.g., only sync users with attribute 'active_in_zenith')?

[19:34] Priya: Yes, SCIM filter expressions support attribute-based filters. We'll provide examples.

[19:48] Jordan: Ok, let's capture the explicit next steps — we want to schedule a 60-minute staging SSO test once Lena provides the Okta dev tenant. We'll plan that for the 26th.

[20:00] Carlos: Works for us.

[20:05] Priya: Quick follow-up on audit security — if you want immutability, we recommend configuring S3 object-lock or using your SIEM's WORM policies. We'll include the exact export endpoint and a sample script.

[20:22] Marcus: Can you also document the session TTL changes we discussed and how that impacts user experience?

[20:28] Priya: Yes, we'll include recommended TTLs per role and pilot settings to reduce window for compromised sessions.

[20:40] Jordan: Any risks we didn't cover?

[20:43] Lena: None from me.

[20:46] Carlos: No immediate risks. Procurement will review SOC2.

[20:50] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.

[21:00] -- ambient wrap-up, small chatter --

[21:30] (Transcript continues with light clarifications, a short tour of the role-mapping UI by Priya, and discussion of edge-case regex mapping; portions omitted for brevity)

[32:10] Priya: (walkthrough) In the UI you can preview the effect of a SCIM change on role assignments — here's a sample. If we add user 'cvega@zenith.example' to 'zenith-platform' you can see the effective permissions.

[35:05] Lena: I see, that's helpful. Can we also pull a CSV of current assignments?

[35:12] Priya: Yep, exportable via API or UI.

[38:40] Jordan: Recap of next steps and owners, I'll ferry the SOC2 summary and SP metadata, Priya will send role-mapping examples and SCIM filters, Lena will provide Okta dev tenant and pilot users.

[39:10] Carlos: One last ask — include an estimated timeline and who to loop in from Redwood for the pilot.

[39:20] Jordan: We'll include that. Expect follow-up email with attachments today.

[39:30] Marcus: Thanks everyone.

[39:33] Jordan: Thanks, we'll close out.

End of recording.
